newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum - Investors in short-term debt are losing out.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum - Investors in short-term debt are losing out.

text.p: Bundesbank vice president Johann Gaddum said on Tuesday that investors holding mainly short-term German debt would lose out in the long-term unless they moved further down the yield curve.

Speaking at a news conference at the Bundesbank, Gaddum said investors shying away from longer-dated bonds because of uncertainty about future developments were missing out on the higher returns such investments could offer by sticking with lower-yielding short-term debt.
Gaddum also said the long-end of the bond market, which tends to be less sensitive to near-term price fluctuations, was attractive for small investors because of its stable nature.
The Bundesbank news conference was called to announce a new 30-year strippable German government bond.
